text:
Hannah Rivera: dropping proposed copy for the Console “Rollback optimization config” flow. Looking for feedback esp on confirmation text + blast radius + accessibility.

Hannah Rivera:
Modal title: “Rollback config?”
Body: “This will rollback Optimize configuration to a previous version. The change will apply immediately and may affect latency/cost.”
Summary panel:
- Scope: {customer}/{deployment} ({Hosted|Dedicated|Private})
- Target: {route} / {model}
- From: v{current} (applied {time})
- To: v{target} (created {time} by {author})
- Blast radius: {regions} / {clusters} / {replicas}
Buttons: [Cancel] [Rollback]
Checkbox (optional): “I understand this may impact traffic.”

Kenji Nakamura: thanks. couple initial notes:
1) title “Rollback config?” is a little generic. can we make it “Rollback Optimize config to v{target}” so users anchor on what will happen.
2) “apply immediately” is scary + not always true with propagation. maybe “begin applying immediately” or “starts rollout now” + we show progress.
3) accessibility: checkbox as a gate is meh (screen readers + muscle memory). prefer a short confirmation line + maybe require a reason field.

Marissa Cole: +1 on reason field. also “may affect latency/cost” reads like marketing. we should be explicit: rollback reverts batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs for this scope.

Dylan Brooks: agree. also “Rollback” button label needs to indicate what. “Rollback now” / “Rollback to v123” reduces misclicks.

Felix Schneider: re blast radius: do we have actual numbers? I can render “Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1” but replicas is fuzzy in Dedicated w/ autoscaling.

Chloe Martin: backend can give:
- list of target regions/clusters
- “estimated affected capacity” as min/max (based on current replica count + autoscaling bounds)
We should avoid “42 replicas” unless we know it’s exact.

Rafael Mendes: from on-call POV: the confirmation needs “what am I rolling back” in plain language and “where” in a single glance. in an incident I’m not reading paragraphs.
Maybe a top line like:
“Revert Optimize config for HelixBank / route /v1/chat/completions / model llama-3.1-70b in us-east-1 + us-west-2.”

Neha Kapoor: +1. also include expected safety rails: do we run preflight on rollback? (I think rollback is “known-good” but still should validate schema + compat). copy should reflect we will verify and stop if it can’t apply.

Hannah Rivera: rollback still runs basic schema/compat checks; it should basically always pass unless version is corrupted/old format. we can add a one-liner.

Tomáš Novák: usability/accessibility notes:
- Don’t use color alone to convey severity (e.g., red text). Provide icon + text, and ensure contrast.
- Keyboard: default focus should be on Cancel, not Rollback.
- Provide an aria-label on the primary action like “Rollback Optimize config to version 123”.
- Avoid “Are you sure” language; it’s not actionable.

Kenji Nakamura: re reason field: recommend:
Label: “Reason (required)”
Helper: “Link incident/ticket (e.g., INC-1234, ENG-4823)”
We can accept plain text + parse for links.
Also add a “View diff” link right in modal so user can sanity check before confirming.

Felix Schneider: +1 “View diff”. also we should show the diff in a read-only panel with copy-to-clipboard for the version ids. for screen readers, the diff panel needs a summary (“12 fields changed”) and the raw JSON is expandable.

Dylan Brooks: for blast radius, can we standardize the terms? “clusters” means different things across Hosted vs Private. maybe always show:
- Environment: Hosted/Dedicated/Private
- Regions
- Deployment targets: {control plane namespace} or {tenant + deployment id}
And optionally “Estimated affected capacity”.

Marissa Cole: also note: enterprise customers asked explicitly “who performed rollback” and “why”. We should capture reason + auto attach actor and timestamp in audit log. copy could mention “This action will be recorded in audit logs.”

Hannah Rivera: ok updated draft based on feedback:
Title: “Rollback Optimize config to v{target}?”
Body (2 sentences max):
“Revert batching/caching/quantization/routing settings for this scope to version v{target}. We’ll start applying the change immediately and show rollout status; this action is recorded in audit logs.”
Scope summary (single line): “{customer} · {deployment} · {route} · {model}”
Blast radius section:
- Regions: …
- Targets: …
- Estimated affected capacity: … (if available)
Reason (required): text box
Links: “View diff” + “View version history”
Buttons: [Cancel] [Rollback to v{target}]

Rafael Mendes: looks good. one more: add callout if rollback is cross-region vs single region (we’ve had folks accidentally roll back global when they meant one region). maybe “Applies to: Global (2 regions)” vs “Single region”.

Chloe Martin: we can compute that from scope. if scope == customer+route+model+global, label “Global”. if scope pinned region, show “Region: us-east-1 only”.

Tomáš Novák: please ensure the “View diff” link is accessible (not just an icon). and for the modal, keep line length reasonable; screen magnifier users suffer with wide summary tables.

Kenji Nakamura: last nit: avoid the word “settings” and use “configuration” consistently (matches docs). also “start applying immediately” could be “start rollout now” (less absolute).

Dylan Brooks: action items:
- Hannah: update copy with “start rollout now”, add “Global vs region” line, make primary CTA “Rollback to vX”.
- Felix: mock diff summary (“X fields changed”) + expandable raw JSON, confirm keyboard nav + focus order.
- Chloe: confirm blast radius fields + exact/estimated semantics so UI labels are honest.

Hannah Rivera: ack. will push updated strings to the PR today and tag @Kenji for a quick review. :thumbsup:

Kenji Nakamura: :thumbsup: please also paste the final strings in the PR description so we can review without pulling branch.

Marissa Cole: thanks all — this is the exact kind of clarity customers asked for in the HelixBank thread. (audit logs mention is key).

Rafael Mendes: +1. if we can get the summary line + global/region callout in, this will reduce fat-finger incidents a lot.
